jobs.title: Senior Security Technical Program Manager
jobs.excerpt: BeyondTrust is a place where you can bring your purpose to life through the work that you do, creating a safer world through our cybersecurity SaaS portfolio.
jobs.description:
BeyondTrust is a place where you can bring your purpose to life through the work that you do, creating a safer world through our cybersecurity SaaS portfolio.

Our culture of flexibility, trust, and continual learning means you will be recognized for your growth and for the impact you make on our success. You will be surrounded by people who challenge, support, and inspire you to be the best version of yourself.

The Role

As a Senior Security Technical Program Manager at BeyondTrust, you will use your technical expertise, business acumen and security domain knowledge to manage and streamline critical CISO Office operations and programs. In this role, you will be an advocate for building seamless and metrics-driven operational frameworks. You will be responsible for working collaboratively with CISO Office teams and business stakeholders to identify operational gaps, document requirements and needs, metrics visualization, and execute programs to streamline the way BeyondTrust build and retains customer trust.

What You’ll Do

  • Oversee, plan, and manage security initiatives for all security pillars.
  • Serve as the Security TPM for the security issues management program, running the end-to-end lifecycle on the security issues management Jira board from identification and triage through handoff, validation, closure, and reporting.
  • Triage every new issues against the priority rubric (exploitability, blast radius, data sensitivity, regulatory or audit linkage, and compensating controls), confirm or adjust the Reporter’s initial priority, and set a due date at triage, hand off to Assignee as identified.
  • Own Critical and High issues day to day, including executive notification, direct engagement with the Assignee, unblocking dependencies, and fast-tracking validation. Monitor additional issues through the recurring security issues management review and step in when an escalation trigger fires.
  • Enforce the analysis gate before handoff, approving a ticket as handoff-ready only when root cause, a specific recommended remediation, named impacted systems and teams, and verifiable acceptance criteria are documented.
  • Identify the correct accountable Assignee by role, run a single structured handoff meeting, and drive formal acceptance in Jira within the agreed window.
  • Confirm Assignee remediation plans meet the acceptance criteria without redesigning them, and help surface cross-team dependencies such as budget, tooling, or other teams.
  • Run the recurring cross-functional security issues review, require an updated due date and logged reason for any slippage, and act as decision-maker on priority and acceptance-criteria disputes, escalating unresolved disagreements to the Sponsor.
  • Formally close security issues only after independent Security validation passes, and reopen failed validations to the Assignee with the specific gap noted.
  • Maintain security issues management board hygiene, including identifying duplicate or overlapping tickets, consolidation opportunities, and tickets missing descriptions, due dates, or owners.
  • Lead the Cloud Governance program to convert eligible cloud-scoped remediations into enforceable Kion guardrails.
  • Create detailed project plans to support each initiative while defining and supporting metric visualization for all of BT.
  • Provide a steady stream of ideas and solutions during security initiatives to introduce innovation and improve operational efficiency.
  • Implement relevant metrics to measure security specific program success, including the security issues management program health (open and closed volume by priority tier, overdue tickets, tickets not yet accepted, and due-date slippage).
  • Develop reports to communicate program progress, including the monthly rollup and the quarterly Sponsor program review, to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with other cross-functional teams.
  • Identify cross-team dependencies to incorporate them into the program planning process.
  • Ensure root cause analysis is completed for technical issues and security findings, and shepherd the implementation of solutions through accountable owners.
  • Make necessary recommendations for adjustments to security processes based on performance metrics.
  • Influence strategic decisions about security direction.
  • Participates in building and managing of AI processes to create operational efficiency.
  • Ensure complete compliance according to industry standards by documenting all the processes and adjusting them, when necessary.
  • Manage project escalations and help assemble project teams to tackle critical items, including executing the security issues management program’s defined escalation triggers (non-acceptance, unlogged slippage, and overdue or Critical findings) to the Assignee’s Manager, Trust & Assurance Leadership, or the ELT Sponsor.

What You’ll Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in technology, Business Administration, Computer Science, or related field
  • 5-7 years of relevant professional experience in security, project management, or technology
  • Proficient level of understanding security domains
  • Experience in communicating technical concepts to non-technical audiences and vice versa.
  • Experience with creative problem solving in a fast-paced and ever-changing environment.
  • Experience in Security or Cloud software solutions
  • Ability to recognize, evaluate and reduce program risks
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills
  • Demonstrated experience running a security findings, vulnerability management, or audit remediation program across multiple engineering and business teams, from intake and prioritization through verified closure
  • Experience applying structured risk-scoring methods (e.g., CVSS or a weighted rubric) consistently and defending prioritization decisions with stakeholders
  • Proven ability to drive accountability with owners outside your reporting line, including formal handoffs, acceptance, and escalation to senior leadership
  • Hands-on experience with Jira workflows, JQL, and dashboards for program tracking and reporting
  • Working knowledge of compliance frameworks and audit evidence (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001)

Nice To Have

  • Security certification, e.g. CISA, CISSP; program management certification, e.g. PMP
  • Strong business acumen
  • Big picture thinker and self-starter
  • Excellent time management and organizational skills
  • Experience working for a fast paced, SaaS company
  • Strong spoken and written communication skills
  • Experience with cloud security posture management or policy-as-code guardrails in AWS, Azure, or GCP (e.g., Kion)
  • Experience using automation or AI to streamline finding triage, validation, or program reporting

Better Together

Diversity. Inclusion. They’re more than just words for us. They are the guiding values of how we build our teams, cultivate leaders, and create a culture where people feel connected.

We take care of our employees so they can take care of our customers. Customers who come from all walks of life just like us. We hire incredible people from diverse backgrounds because when we are different together, we are stronger together.

About Us

BeyondTrust is the global identity security leader protecting Paths to Privilege™. Our identity-centric approach goes beyond securing privileges and access, empowering organizations with the most effective solution to manage the entire identity attack surface and neutralize threats, whether from external attacks or insiders.

BeyondTrust is leading the charge in transforming identity security to prevent breaches and limit the blast radius of attacks, while creating a superior customer experience and operational efficiencies. We are trusted by 20,000 customers, including 75 of the Fortune 100, and our global ecosystem of partners.

jobs.description:
IMI plc
We are a global specialist engineering company that creates breakthrough solutions. We are curious and like to solve problems, partnering with our customers to solve the demands of today and prepare for the challenges of tomorrow. We embrace innovation and care about outcomes that are good for business, everyday life and making a better world – creating lasting impact for everyone.

We design, build and service highly engineered products in fluid and motion control applications. We focus on five market sectors: Industrial Automation, Process Automation, Climate Control, Life Science and Fluid Control, and Transport.

Instrumentation
Instrumentation goes to market with IMI’s range of high integrity instrumentation products for offshore oil and gas platforms, refineries and chemical plants. Our precision components are at the heart of the energy and chemical industry’s most marvellous machines – with market leading fluid control products tackling the most extreme operating conditions and engineering challenges on the planet.

At the heart of our offering are Actuators, Positioners Final Control elements like solenoid valves, air preparation equipment, pneumatic and hydraulic pressure switches, I/P and E/P convertors, redundant valve manifold systems (RVM) and cutting edge Industrial IoT monitoring solutions.

Role Overview
As an Electronics Hardware Engineer (ATEX / IECEx), you will design and validate Industrial IoT hardware for use in hazardous (Ex) environments, supporting IMI TWTG’s wireless sensing and connectivity solutions.

You will take ownership of electronic designs from concept through to production, including schematic and PCB design, radio integration and sensor development. Working in a multidisciplinary team alongside firmware, mechanical and data engineers, you will help deliver robust, certified products that operate reliably in demanding industrial environments such as oil & gas, chemicals and heavy industry.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop hardware designs for Industrial IoT products from requirements through to implementation
  • Design with a strong focus on intrinsically safe (Ex ia) architectures, actively supporting compliance and certification activities
  • Create schematics and PCB layouts in Altium, including radio transceiver and sensor designs
  • Plan and execute verification activities, including test plans, board bring‑up, troubleshooting and reporting
  • Maintain clear and accurate technical documentation, including design files, BOMs and change records
  • Write and maintain documentation required for ATEX, IECEx and product certification
  • Act as the technical point of contact for test houses and notified bodies covering radio, EMC and Ex certification

Critical Competencies for Success

  • Bachelor’s level of working and thinking (HBO) through education and/or relevant experience
  • 4+ years of relevant experience in electronics hardware development
  • Proven experience designing electronics for hazardous or Ex‑regulated environments
  • Hands‑on experience with ATEX / IECEx certification projects
  • Experience supporting product certification activities such as RED, FCC and UKCA
  • Strong experience with Altium for schematic capture and PCB layout, including versioning and document control (Altium 365)
  • Comfortable working primarily with digital designs, with supporting analog circuitry for power management and sensor front‑ends
  • Structured, proactive and communicative way of working
  • Ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary Scrum team, planning work and managing risks proactively
  • Ability to read, write and speak English fluently

Diserable Competencies

  • Hands‑on experience with low‑power wireless design for Industrial IoT applications
  • Experience with LoRaWAN‑based products and ST / ARM microcontrollers
  • Experience with Ex ma (encapsulation) design approaches
  • Experience integrating MEMS sensors
  • Interest in expanding technical ownership or taking on limited project coordination responsibilities
  • Ability to read, write and speak Dutch

jobs.description:
At Caris, we understand that cancer is an ugly word—a word no one wants to hear, but one that connects us all. That’s why we’re not just transforming cancer care—we’re changing lives.

We introduced precision medicine to the world and built an industry around the idea that every patient deserves answers as unique as their DNA. Backed by cutting-edge molecular science and AI, we ask ourselves every day:“What would I do if this patient were my mom?”That question drives everything we do.

But our mission doesn’t stop with cancer. We're pushing the frontiers of medicine and leading a revolution in healthcare—driven by innovation, compassion, and purpose.

Join us in our mission to improve the human condition across multiple diseases. If you're passionate about meaningful work and want to be part of something bigger than yourself, Caris is where your impact begins.

Position Summary

The Account Executive – MI Clarity is responsible for driving awareness, adoption, and utilization of MI Clarity, an AI-powered prognostic assay designed to assess both early and late distant recurrence risk in postmenopausal patients with HR-positive/HER2-negative, node-negative early-stage breast cancer.

The Account Executive will partner with oncologists, breast surgeons, pathologists, nurse navigators, and healthcare systems to educate stakeholders on the clinical value of the test, integrate the assay into clinical workflows, and increase appropriate utilization.

This role requires a strong understanding of oncology, breast cancer treatment pathways, molecular diagnostics, and value-based clinical conversations. Success is measured through account engagement, clinician adoption, testing utilization, and long-term strategic growth.

Job Responsibilities

  • Educate healthcare providers and care teams on the clinical utility, prognostic value, and evidence supporting MI Clarity, including its ability to identify both early and late distant recurrence risk in eligible breast cancer patients.

  • Present clinical data, validation studies, and evidence-based insights, while explaining the differentiation of AI-driven pathology analysis from traditional genomic and molecular assays.

  • Conduct in-person and virtual educational programs and lead consultative, evidence-based discussions on risk stratification, treatment planning, extended endocrine therapy considerations, and opportunities to reduce overtreatment and undertreatment.

  • Position MI Clarity as a clinical decision-support tool that optimizes patient care, addressing questions related to assay performance, patient selection, workflow integration, turnaround time, and clinical interpretation.

  • Develop and execute strategic territory and account plans to drive awareness, adoption, and utilization of MI Clarity.

  • Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, including medical oncologists, breast surgeons, pathologists, advanced practice providers, nurse navigators, health system administrators, and other clinical decision-makers.

  • Identify and engage key opinion leaders, decision-makers, and clinical champions within target accounts to support adoption and long-term utilization.

  • Support implementation of testing workflows and operational integration within healthcare systems and clinical practices.

  • Analyze territory and account performance data to identify growth opportunities, monitor utilization and adoption trends, and develop targeted engagement strategies.

  • Maintain accurate CRM documentation, forecasting, and account activity records.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Medical Affairs, Marketing, Operations, Customer Support, and other internal teams to support customer success and business objectives.

  • Ensure all activities are conducted in compliance with company policies, healthcare regulations, and industry standards, maintaining accurate, balanced, and approved clinical and promotional communications.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree required; life sciences or healthcare-related field preferred.

  • 3+ years of successful sales experience in one or more of the following: Oncology, Diagnostics, Molecular Testing, Pathology, Medical Device, Pharmaceutical sales

  • Strong understanding of breast cancer treatment pathways and oncology terminology.

  • Proven ability to build relationships with healthcare providers and health systems.

  • Excellent presentation, communication, and consultative selling skills.

  • Ability to interpret and communicate clinical data.

  • Ability to travel within assigned territory.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience selling oncology diagnostics or precision medicine solutions.

  • Existing relationships within oncology or breast centers.

  • Experience launching new products or assays.

  • Familiarity with pathology workflows and digital pathology.

  • Knowledge of prognostic and predictive breast cancer assays.

  • Provider engagement and educational activity

  • Successful workflow implementation within target accounts

  • Territory growth and market penetration

  • CRM accuracy and activity execution

Physical Demands

  • Ability to sit or stand for extended periods.

  • Ability to lift routine office materials.

Additional Information

  • Travel required, including possible evenings, weekends, or holidays.

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world!

Facebook Ads Specialist

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S Business Hours

About the Role

We’re looking for a Facebook Ads Specialist to take ownership of Facebook advertising campaigns from strategy and setup through ongoing optimization. You’ll manage campaign performance, audiences, budgets, testing, and reporting while working closely with the marketing team to improve results.

What You’ll Own

Campaign Planning & Strategy

  • Design and build Facebook ad campaigns from the ground up.
  • Align targeting, creative direction, and budget allocation with business objectives.

Ad Execution & Management

  • Set up, launch, and actively manage Facebook campaigns.
  • Monitor delivery, pacing, and performance on an ongoing basis.

Audience Development

  • Research, build, and refine audience segments.
  • Use custom audiences, lookalikes, and interest-based targeting to improve reach and relevance.

Performance Analysis & Reporting

  • Track key metrics across active campaigns.
  • Analyze campaign data and identify trends.
  • Turn findings into clear recommendations for improving performance.

Creative Collaboration

  • Work with the marketing team to brief, review, and iterate on ad creatives and copy.
  • Ensure assets are optimized for their placement and campaign objective.

Budget Management

  • Manage daily and monthly ad spend responsibly.
  • Adjust bids and budgets to meet efficiency targets without overspending.

Testing & Optimization

  • Run structured A/B tests across audiences, creatives, and landing page combinations.
  • Apply learnings systematically across campaigns.

Required Experience & Skills

  • Proven hands-on experience planning and running Facebook ad campaigns, ideally in a marketing agency or similarly fast-moving environment.
  • Strong command of Meta Ads Manager, including campaign structure, pixel setup, conversion tracking, and attribution settings.
  • Experience managing ad budgets and being accountable for performance results.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret campaign data and identify trends.
  • Experience with A/B testing and a disciplined approach to applying campaign learnings.
  • Confident communication skills with the ability to present performance updates and recommendations clearly.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You take ownership of campaign outcomes from launch through optimization.
  • You’re comfortable working independently in a remote environment.
  • You communicate proactively and flag issues early.
  • You make decisions based on data rather than assumptions or habits.
  • You’re detail-oriented while keeping the broader campaign strategy in focus.

What Success Looks Like

  • Campaigns are launched with clear targeting, creative direction, and budget strategy.
  • Campaign performance is consistently monitored and optimized.
  • Ad spend is managed responsibly against performance targets.
  • A/B testing generates actionable insights that improve campaign results.
  • The marketing team receives clear, useful performance updates and recommendations.

Typical Day

Your day centers on the Focusmediahouse ad accounts. You’ll start by reviewing overnight performance across live campaigns and identifying opportunities for budget adjustments, creative changes, or targeting improvements.

You may then prepare performance reports, brief a designer on a new creative concept, or build the structure for an upcoming campaign. Testing is an ongoing part of the role, including reviewing active experiments, deciding what to scale or cut, and setting up the next round.

Most collaboration happens asynchronously, so strong written communication and clear documentation are important.

  1. Recruiter Screening
  2. Client Interview
  3. Final Selection

At Allegion, we help keep the people you know and love safe and secure where they live, work and visit. With more than 40 brands, 14,000+ employees globally and products sold in 130 countries, we specialize in security around the doorway and beyond.

The IT Business Analyst – Supply Chain is responsible for analyzing, defining, and delivering robust technology solutions that support end-to-end supply chain operations and overarching business goals. In this role, you will bridge the gap between operations and IT by translating business process requirements, championing supply chain data governance, and integrating our core ERP (Microsoft Dynamics 365 F&O / AX 2012) with specialized ancillary supply chain platforms. You will act as a trusted partner to global Supply Chain teams, helping standardize and optimize workflows across procurement, inventory, warehouse management, quality, compliance, and material planning.

Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United States. The company does not intend to provide sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B, TN, etc.) for this employment position.


Remote:


At Allegion, we recognize that great talent and breakthrough ideas can come from anywhere. That’s why this position offers a flexible remote work arrangement, with occasional on-site visits as needed based on the role. Whether you’re working remotely or collaborating in person, we’re committed to providing the tools, support, and dynamic environment you need to succeed. At Allegion, your career thrives where innovation meets flexibility, empowering you to achieve your goals while maintaining a healthy work-life balance.


While this is the current structure and we currently have no plans to change, we reserve the right to make changes to the remote schedule as needed at the Company’s discretion.

What You Will Do:

As a Supply Chain IT Business Analyst, you will bridge the gap between business operations and technology by collaborating with cross-functional leaders to define requirements, streamline processes, and design scalable, future-state solutions aligned with global business strategies. Serving as a functional expert for Microsoft Dynamics 365 F&O / AX, you will author Functional Design Documents (FDDs), configure core supply chain modules—prioritizing out-of-the-box functionality—and work alongside technical developers to build custom extensions and integration points. You will evaluate and integrate third-party ancillary systems (such as demand planning tools and supplier portals) to boost end-to-end supply chain visibility. Additionally, you will champion data governance across master data entities (Item Master, BOMs, Vendor Master), utilizing SQL and Power BI to troubleshoot anomalies, validate data flows, and provide actionable business insights.   • Experience: 3+ years of experience as an IT Business Analyst supporting large manufacturing, distribution, or multi-national supply chain operations.
  • ERP Experience: 3+ years of functional experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations or AX 2012.
  • Domain & Process Knowledge: Demonstrated functional expertise across several (not all required) of the following core supply chain process pillars:
    • Procurement & Sourcing: Purchase Requisitions, Purchase Orders (PO), and Vendor Master management
    • Master Data Management: Item Master, Bill of Materials (BOM) creation/maintenance, and data governance
    • Warehouse & Inventory Control: Receiving (WMS), Cycle Counting, and Physical Inventory (PI) procedures
    • External & Partner Operations: Outside Vendor/Service Operations (OSV), and Supplier-Owned / Managed Inventory (SOMI / VMI)
    • Planning & Quality: Demand Forecasting, Product Quality & Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) workflows
    • Compliance: Global Trade Compliance and regulatory transaction tracking
  • Ancillary Software & Integrations: Experience supporting integrations with peripheral supply chain applications
  • Communication & Collaboration: Exceptional communication skills with the ability to lead workshops, present to senior stakeholders, and collaborate with technical development teams.

Preferred:

  • Experience participating in global, multi-region ERP implementations, rollouts, or major version upgrades.
  • Working knowledge of relational databases and basic-to-intermediate SQL skills for ad-hoc data analysis and validation.
  • Knowledge of BI tools (e.g., Power BI) for supply chain metrics and dashboard creation.
  • Familiarity with structured implementation methodologies

Work Environment & Travel:

  • Travel: Approximately 10%-20% travel required (site visits, project milestones, go-live support).

Allegion is a Great Place to Grow your Career if:

  • You're seeking a rewarding opportunity that allows you to truly help others. With thousands of employees and customers around the world, there’s plenty of room to make an impact. As our values state, “this is your business, run with it”.
  • You’re looking for a company that will invest in your professional development. As we grow, we want you to grow with us.

  • Employee Discounts through Perks at Work
  • Community involvement and opportunities to give back so you can “serve others, not yourself”
  • Opportunities to leverage your unique strengths through Clifton Strengths assessment & coaching


Apply Today!

Join our team of experts today and help us make tomorrow’s world a safer place!

Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification and every single preferred qualification of a job posting. jobs.description:
Call Center Agent / Mitarbeiter Telefonvertrieb (m/w/d) – 100 % Homeoffice

Teilzeit (ab 30 Stunden) oder Vollzeit | Montag bis Freitag | unbefristete Festanstellung

Telefonieren liegt Ihnen? Dann machen Sie daraus Ihren Job – von zu Hause aus.

Sie sprechen gerne mit Menschen, können sich gut ausdrücken und suchen eine Tätigkeit, die sich dauerhaft aus dem Homeoffice erledigen lässt?

Für unseren Mandanten, ein etabliertes Unternehmen mit professioneller Vertriebsorganisation, suchen wir Verstärkung im telefonischen Kundenkontakt.

Ihre Aufgabe ist klar: Sie kommen mit Gewerbekunden ins Gespräch, erkennen Interesse und vereinbaren qualifizierte Termine für den Außendienst. Sie müssen dabei keine Verträge am Telefon abschließen. Stattdessen schaffen Sie den ersten guten Kontakt und unterstützen damit direkt den Vertriebserfolg.

Dabei arbeiten Sie mit klar definierten Zielgruppen, professionellen Gesprächsleitfäden und strukturierten Prozessen. Die Terminvereinbarung mit potenziellen Interessenten und bestehenden Kunden bildet den Schwerpunkt der Tätigkeit.

Das erwartet Sie in Ihrem Arbeitsalltag

  • Sie sprechen Geschäftskunden aktiv telefonisch an und kommen mit ihnen ins Gespräch.

  • Sie vereinbaren Termine für die Kolleginnen und Kollegen im Außendienst.

  • Sie kontaktieren sowohl potenzielle Neukunden als auch bestehende Kunden.

  • Sie arbeiten mit einem erprobten Gesprächsleitfaden und klar definierten Zielgruppen.

  • Sie dokumentieren Ihre Gespräche zuverlässig im CRM-System.

  • Sie unterstützen die Termin- und Routenplanung des Außendienstes.

  • Sie arbeiten digital und eng mit Ihrem Team zusammen.

Neben der Telefonie gehören CRM-Datenpflege und organisatorische Aufgaben zum Stellenprofil.

Requirements

Was Sie mitbringen sollten

Sie müssen keinen perfekten Vertriebslebenslauf haben.

Viel wichtiger ist, dass Sie gerne telefonieren, offen auf Menschen zugehen und sich durch ein „Nein“ nicht sofort aus der Ruhe bringen lassen.

Besonders gut passen Erfahrungen aus dem Call Center, Telefonvertrieb, Kundenservice, Vertriebsinnendienst oder der Terminvereinbarung. Aber auch Bewerberinnen und Bewerber aus Hotellerie, Gesundheitswesen, Büromanagement, Assistenz oder anderen kundenorientierten Tätigkeiten können gut zu dieser Position passen.

Sie sollten außerdem sicher Deutsch sprechen und schreiben, mit gängiger Bürosoftware umgehen können und selbstständig sowie zuverlässig im Homeoffice arbeiten.

Noch keine klassische Outbound-Erfahrung? Wenn Sie gerne telefonieren, kommunikativ sind und bereit sind, aktiv auf Geschäftskunden zuzugehen, freuen wir uns ebenfalls auf Ihre Bewerbung.

Darauf können Sie sich freuen

100 % Homeoffice

Nach Ihrer Einarbeitung arbeiten Sie dauerhaft von zu Hause – unabhängig davon, wo Sie in Deutschland wohnen.

Planbare Arbeitszeiten

Die Position ist bereits ab 30 Stunden pro Woche möglich. Die Arbeitszeit liegt montags bis freitags im Tagesbereich – aktuell bei 30 Stunden beispielsweise von 8:00 bis 14:30 Uhr inklusive Pause.

Unbefristete Festanstellung

Sie werden direkt bei unserem Mandanten eingestellt. Keine Zeitarbeit, keine Arbeitnehmerüberlassung.

Attraktives Vergütungsmodell

Sie erhalten ein festes Gehalt sowie eine zusätzliche variable Vergütung. Das Fixum wird 13-mal jährlich gezahlt. Für die ersten neun Monate gibt es eine Garantieprovision, damit Sie in Ruhe in der neuen Aufgabe ankommen können.

Struktur statt Sprung ins kalte Wasser

Sie erhalten klare Prozesse, Gesprächsleitfäden, digitale Arbeitsmittel und eine professionelle Einarbeitung.

Keine Wochenend- oder Schichtarbeit

Die Tätigkeit findet regulär von Montag bis Freitag statt.

Ihre Einarbeitung in Hannover

Damit Sie anschließend sicher und selbstständig aus dem Homeoffice arbeiten können, lernen Sie zu Beginn die Aufgaben, Abläufe und Systeme persönlich kennen. Dafür findet eine ca. zweiwöchige Einarbeitung in Hannover statt. Die Kosten für die notwendige Anreise und Unterbringung werden übernommen. Danach arbeiten Sie dauerhaft im Homeoffice.

Für wen ist die Position besonders interessant?

Vielleicht arbeiten Sie heute bereits als Call Center Agent, Kundenberater, Mitarbeiter im Kundenservice oder Telefonvertrieb.

Vielleicht kommen Sie aber auch aus einer Arztpraxis, einem Hotel, einem Büro, einer Assistenzfunktion oder einer anderen Tätigkeit mit viel Kundenkontakt. Entscheidend ist nicht Ihre bisherige Stellenbezeichnung.

Entscheidend ist, dass Sie gerne kommunizieren und Lust darauf haben, Menschen am Telefon für ein Gespräch mit dem Außendienst zu gewinnen.

Klingt nach einem Job, der zu Ihnen passen könnte?

Dann machen wir es Ihnen einfach.

Bewerben Sie sich direkt mit Ihrem Lebenslauf. Ein Anschreiben benötigen wir nicht.

Im nächsten Schritt stellen wir Ihnen einige kurze Fragen zu Ihrer bisherigen Telefonerfahrung, Ihren Arbeitszeiten und der Einarbeitung in Hannover.

Wir, die persoperm GmbH, vermitteln ausschließlich in unbefristete Festanstellungen bei unseren Mandanten. Für Sie als Bewerberin oder Bewerber ist unsere Dienstleistung selbstverständlich vollständig kostenfrei.

Wir freuen uns darauf, Sie kennenzulernen.

Highlights

100 % Homeoffice,30–40 Std. pro Woche und freie Wochenenden: Nutzen Sie Ihre Kommunikationsstärke im telefonischen B2B-Kundenkontakt – mit strukturierter Einarbeitung und Festanstellung.

jobs.title: Senior AI Engineer, Agentic Platform
jobs.excerpt: We are looking for a product-minded AI engineer to turn what our customers are trying to decide into agents they actually rely on.
jobs.description:
We are looking for a product-minded AI engineer to turn what our customers are trying to decide into agents they actually rely on. AskWaive, our in-product assistant, is already live; the work now is quality, coverage, and an experience that wows.

This is not a role for a prompt author or a demo builder. We want an owner: someone who takes a customer need—already expressed through our serving layers and semantic layer—and turns it into an endpoint, a tool, and an experience that makes the customer measurably better at their job. Agent engineering, deployment, and testing are all part of delivery, not a handoff.

Our core data platform is owned by the team that built it. You'll build on top of it—and where data or infrastructure is holding an agent back, you'll have the standing to propose the change and drive it.

What You'll Do

    From Customer Need to Product Superpower

    • Own the Outcome: Start from the customer, and stay with it until the agent is answering their needs better

    • Build Agents and Tools: Build production agents and the tools they call—retrieval, multi-step workflows, action-taking—on Amazon Bedrock, with Bedrock AgentCore as our runtime and tools exposed over MCP (Model Context Protocol).

    • Turn Serving Layers Into Capability: Our semantic layer and service APIs are where customer needs are already expressed. Your job is turning them into endpoints and tools an agent can wield well—and knowing which metrics and entities it should reach at all.

    • Shape the Experience, Not Just the Endpoint: How an answer arrives—its speed, its confidence, its explanation, the next step it offers—is the product. A technically correct response a customer ignores is a failure.

      • Prove It and Make It Felt

      • Measure Groundedness: Build the eval harness—labeled test sets, groundedness and hallucination rates you can put a number on, and CI gates that stop a regression before it ships.

      • Measure What Customers Got: Adoption, feedback, intent—then report realized impact back to Product and the business in numbers that hold up.

      • Diagnose and Iterate: Instrument the tracing that shows why an answer was wrong, turn each failure mode into a specific fix, and ship again. This loop is the job, not a phase of it.

        • Deliver

        • Ship and Operate: Own the serving path—MCP endpoints, latency, cost per response, caching, and runtime guardrails. Deployment and testing are part of the job, not a handoff.

        • Embed and Influence: Partner with Product Managers and engineers on which decisions an agent should support—and which it shouldn't. Where data or infrastructure limits what an agent can do, drive the change alongside the team that owns the platform.

Who You Are

    The Owner: You measure your work by whether customers made better decisions with the agent's help, not by whether it shipped.

    The Agent Builder: You've taken an agent past the demo. You know the hard part is everything after it works once—coverage, grounding, cost, and the failure modes you only see at scale. You fix problems without waiting for a ticket.

    The Experience Obsessive: You care how an answer lands, not just whether it was right. Trustworthy, fast, and legible beats clever.

    We know that great talent comes from many backgrounds. If you are a builder who cares about the "why" behind the code, we want to hear from you!

    HOW WE WORK

    We build with coding agents. You set direction and targets, review output critically, and build the harnesses—scaffolding, context, tests, review loops—that make the next task faster for the whole team. The leverage is in the verification: the tests, CI gates, and typed interfaces that make agent-written code safe to merge.

What You"ll Bring

    • Experience: 5+ years building production software or data-intensive systems used by real customers, with strong Python skills—including at least one LLM or agent feature you shipped to production users.

    • AWS & Agent Stack: Hands-on AWS experience, ideally Amazon Bedrock and Bedrock AgentCore. Equivalent agent runtimes transfer, but we build on AWS and you'll be productive faster if you have prior exposure.

    • Agent Engineering: Orchestration, tool and function design, context assembly, and multi-step workflows—you've made the design calls, not just the prompt calls.

    • Retrieval & Domain Grounding: You've built retrieval over real business data, you can explain how context gets selected and why an answer was wrong, and you have enough SQL and metric fluency to catch an agent answering with the wrong number.

    • Evaluation & Iteration: You've built or owned an eval loop for a generative system—labelled sets, regression gates, and a number you could defend when someone asked whether it got better.

    • Product Sense for AI: You have opinions about how an agent should behave—when to answer, when to ask, when to refuse, how to show its work—and you've shipped those opinions, not just argued them.

    • Measurement & Narrative: You've quantified what an agent actually delivered for users—adoption, task success, decision quality—and presented it to people who were never going to read your traces.

    • Working With Agents: You've used coding agents on real production work, you can tell correct output from merely plausible output, and you invest in the harnesses that make the next task faster.

    • Communication & Collaboration: Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with a track record of working across technical and non-technical teams.

      • Bonus Points For:

      • LLM observability tooling (Langfuse, LangSmith, or Arize).

      • Semantic layer or metrics-layer design (Ossie, dbt).

      • Field-service, logistics, or other operational SaaS domains.

      • Prior experience as a senior or lead engineer responsible for guiding technical direction.


        • Location: Remote (UK-based) with occasional collaborative team meetups.

        Right to Work: Applicants must currently have the legal right to work in the UK. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position at this time.

WHAT YOU SHOULD KNOW ABOUT US

  • Laid back but focused: We offer a flexible, collaborative work environment and a passion for developing innovative, best-in-class solutions that directly contribute to the success of our customers.

  • Impact-driven: We care deeply and deliver services and solutions that make a real difference in the lives of our clients and their businesses.

  • Trust & Inclusion: We openly accept others as they are and build strong partnerships based on trust and mutual respect.

RELAX, WE'VE GOT YOU COVERED

  • Competitive company pension scheme with employer match.

  • Generous holiday allowance / flexible time off plus UK bank holidays.

  • Enhanced maternity, paternity, and parental leave policies.

  • Ongoing learning resources.

  • Comprehensive Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) providing free 24/7 mental health, legal, and financial guidance.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

WorkWave is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees in accordance with the Equality Act 2010.

Don't meet every single requirement? Studies show that women and underrepresented groups are less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every qualification. If you feel you could make a great impact in this role, we encourage you to apply anyway!

As a member of Experian's Global Security Office (EGSO), the Senior Enterprise Security Incident Manager (ESIM) serves as the Cyber Incident Commander for significant cybersecurity incidents, leading cross-functional response efforts across the enterprise

This hands-on technical role coordinates the full incident response lifecycle, from detection and containment through recovery and post-incident analysis, while providing executive-level communications, driving operational decision-making, and ensuring alignment with Experian's Global Information Security Incident Response Plan.

You will report to the CFC Senior Director of Incident Response as part of Experian's Cyber Fusion Center. As an individual contributor, you will partner with technical teams, business leaders, and executives. Your goals will be to minimize business impact, strengthen incident readiness, and improve our cyber resilience.

Must be available to respond to after-hours pages for potentially major security incidents and manage the CFC incident response during assigned nights, weekends, and holidays as part of an on-call rotation.

You'll have the opportunity to:

  • Lead enterprise-wide response to high-risk cybersecurity incidents as Cyber Incident Commander, validating and escalating incidents, directing cross-functional response efforts, and driving containment, eradication, recovery, and resolution.
  • Provide executive incident leadership by delivering updates to senior leaders and stakeholders, coordinating technical and business teams, supporting decision-making, and maintaining accurate incident documentation.
  • Enhance the incident response program through post-incident reviews, root cause analysis, lessons learned, and continuous improvements to response plans, playbooks, and operational processes.
  • Strengthen cyber readiness by leading tabletop exercises, partnering with business and technology stakeholders to validate response capabilities, identify gaps, and improve preparedness.
  • Support Cyber Fusion Center operations by maintaining awareness of emerging threats, collaborating across security and technology teams, participating in the on-call rotation, and contributing to plans that strengthen Experian's security posture.

Your background:

  • 8+ years of experience in security operations or information technology, with 5+ years in information security incident handling or response.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Security, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Experience leading/supporting investigations and response to complex cybersecurity incidents, including APTs, ransomware, DDoS, insider threats, web/mobile application attacks, and data exfiltration.
  • Knowledge of cyber incident response, digital investigation methodologies, and adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), including incident triage, impact assessment, containment, remediation, and recovery.
  • Broad technical knowledge of enterprise and cloud environments, including operating systems, networking, security controls, enterprise technologies, and detection and response platforms.
  • Experience investigating complex incidents, performing root cause analysis, making risk-based decisions, and communicating technical findings to all audiences.
  • Leadership experience coordinating cross-functional incident response activities, influencing stakeholders, and managing multiple high-priority cybersecurity incidents.
  • Demonstrated initiative, including the ability to identify improvement opportunities, drive security enhancements, and operate effectively while keeping leadership informed.
  • Plus: Industry certifications in cybersecurity, incident response, digital forensics, or ethical hacking preferred (e.g., GIAC, CISSP, SSCP, CISM, EC-Council, Offensive Security).

Executive Support | Calendar Management | Travel Coordination | Remote

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours (Flexibility Required)

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring a highly organized and proactive Executive Assistant (EA) to provide strategic administrative and operational support to senior leadership.

This is more than a traditional administrative role. You’ll serve as a trusted partner, helping executives stay focused on high-impact priorities by managing calendars, coordinating travel, handling executive communications, preparing meetings, and ensuring projects and follow-ups move forward seamlessly.

If you thrive in fast-paced environments, anticipate needs before they arise, and excel at keeping executives organized and productive, this role is an excellent opportunity.

What You’ll Own

Calendar & Scheduling Management

  • Manage complex executive calendars across multiple time zones.
  • Coordinate meetings, calls, travel, and scheduling priorities.
  • Resolve scheduling conflicts and optimize executive availability.
  • Utilize Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook, Calendly, and related scheduling tools.
  • Ensure executives are fully prepared for upcoming meetings and commitments.

Executive Communication & Support

  • Draft, proofread, and send professional emails and executive communications.
  • Manage executive inboxes, prioritizing urgent requests and correspondence.
  • Screen calls, messages, and meeting requests.
  • Serve as a liaison between executives, clients, vendors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Handle confidential information with professionalism and discretion.

Meeting Preparation & Follow-Up

  • Prepare meeting agendas, briefing documents, presentations, and talking points.
  • Gather and organize supporting materials before meetings.
  • Take meeting notes, document action items, and track follow-ups.
  • Ensure deadlines, priorities, and deliverables remain on schedule.

Travel & Logistics Coordination

  • Coordinate domestic and international travel arrangements.
  • Book flights, hotels, transportation, and complete travel itineraries.
  • Manage last-minute schedule changes and travel adjustments.
  • Track travel expenses and assist with reimbursements.
  • Ensure seamless travel logistics for executives.

Project & Administrative Support

  • Track executive priorities, projects, and ongoing initiatives.
  • Follow up with internal teams to ensure deliverables and deadlines are met.
  • Conduct research and prepare reports, summaries, and briefing materials.
  • Maintain organized digital filing systems and documentation.
  • Support operational initiatives and special projects as assigned.

Requirements

Must-Have Qualifications

Experience

  • 3+ years of Executive Assistant or senior administrative support experience.
  • Experience supporting executives in fast-paced business environments.
  • Proven experience managing complex calendars across multiple time zones.
  • Experience coordinating executive travel and logistics.

Technical Skills

  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and Microsoft Office.
  • Strong experience using calendar and scheduling tools.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Outstanding organizational, multitasking, and time management abilities.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information professionally.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience supporting startups, agencies, consulting firms, or high-growth organizations.
  • Familiarity with Slack, Zoom, Notion, Asana, ClickUp, or similar collaboration platforms.
  • Experience supporting multiple executives simultaneously.
  • Exposure to operations, project coordination, or business support functions.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • Exceptionally organized with outstanding attention to detail.
  • Proactive and able to anticipate executive needs.
  • Strong communicator who builds trust across teams and stakeholders.
  • Calm under pressure and adaptable to changing priorities.
  • Highly dependable with excellent follow-through.
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

  • Review executive calendars and prepare daily briefing notes.
  • Manage inboxes, scheduling requests, and executive communications.
  • Coordinate meetings, agendas, and follow-up actions.
  • Arrange travel plans and manage logistics.
  • Track project updates and ensure priorities stay on schedule.
  • Prepare reports, summaries, and next-day planning materials.

In short: You enable executives to operate at peak efficiency by managing schedules, communication, travel, and operational priorities with accuracy and professionalism.

Key Metrics for Success (KPIs)

  • Calendar accuracy and scheduling efficiency.
  • Timely communication and follow-up completion.
  • Executive satisfaction with operational support.
  • Smooth travel coordination and logistics management.
  • Reduction in scheduling conflicts and administrative delays.
  • Accuracy and organization of executive documentation.

Why Join Us?

  • Fully remote opportunity aligned with U.S. business hours.
  • High-visibility role supporting senior leadership directly.
  • Opportunity to work closely with decision-makers and executives.
  • Fast-paced, collaborative, and growth-oriented environment.
  • Exposure to executive operations, strategic initiatives, and business management.
  • Career growth opportunities into Operations, Project Management, Chief of Staff, or Executive Operations roles.

Interview Process

  1. Initial Phone Screen
  2. Spark Hire Intro Video (3–5 minutes)
  3. Practical Assessment (Executive Briefing Memo or Scheduling Scenario)
  4. Client Interview

jobs.title: Account Executive, Mid-Market
jobs.excerpt: Somewhere in your career, you closed a deal that wasn't supposed to close.
jobs.description:
Somewhere in your career, you closed a deal that wasn't supposed to close. You read the room before anyone else did. You qualified hard when it would have been easier to keep the deal warm. You pushed when the prospect was drifting and held your ground when they pushed back on price. And when it closed, it closed because of how you ran it — not because the lead was good.

That's the kind of Account Executive we're looking for.

What We Do

Every school district in America runs on service — parents need answers, teachers need support, IT teams need systems that work. Most districts cobble that together with disconnected tools, overwhelmed staff, and no real visibility into what's working.

Onflo built the platform that fixes that. Our unified service platform brings together customer service, help desk ticketing, call center operations, AI chat, and IT asset management — purpose-built for K-12 public education. When a district runs on Onflo, their staff spends less time firefighting and more time serving students.

That's the product you'll be selling. It's a good one. And the people who buy it — superintendents, IT directors, operations leaders — are trying to do something that matters.

The Role

You'll own a territory. Not work it — own it. New business quota, pipeline coverage, and the strategy underneath both. You'll know which districts are ready, which are warming, and which aren't worth your time — and you'll act accordingly. You'll source your own pipeline, run your own cycles, and close your own deals. When Marketing helps, great. When they don't, you still hit your number.

What you'll own:

  • New business quota attainment in a defined K-12 geographic territory
  • Self-sourced pipeline at 3–5x quota coverage
  • Full sales cycle: prospecting, discovery, demo, negotiation, close
  • Forecast accuracy you can defend in any deal review
  • Executive relationships across districts in your territory

Who Thrives Here

We'll be direct with you, because we think you'll appreciate it.

Onflo is a small, entrepreneurial team. We don't have a perfect playbook for everything. Priorities shift. Conversations can be intense. Communication isn't always tidy. Marketing won't always feed you the lead flow you want. Product won't always ship on the timeline you'd hope. We know that — and we're actively working on it. What we do have is a product that genuinely helps schools, clients who trust us, and a team that cares about doing the work well.

The people who do their best work here own their outcomes completely — no waiting, no excuses, no "the leads weren't there." They stay calm when priorities shift, build their own pipeline when the inbound is thin, and hold themselves to a higher standard than anyone else would set for them. They're direct without being harsh, coachable without being passive, and motivated by winning more than recognition. They ask for the meeting, ask for the demo, and ask for the close. They don't reflexively discount when a prospect pushes back on price. And underneath all of it, they genuinely care — about the districts they sell to, about the teammates next to them, and about doing the work right.

If you've spent your career waiting for clear direction, clean territory, and steady inbound flow before you produce — this probably isn't your role. If you've spent it figuring it out and hitting your number anyway — keep reading.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of B2B SaaS sales managing a full sales cycle, with a track record of quota attainment or overachievement
  • Demonstrated ability to self-source pipeline — not just work inbound or SDR-fed leads
  • Comfortable in every part of the cycle, especially the hard parts: qualifying out, holding price, asking for the close
  • Technically curious — you learn new software by getting in and clicking around, and you can hold your own with an IT director without a Solutions Engineer in the room
  • Active Salesforce user and AI tool adopter
  • K-12 or EdTech experience is a plus, not a requirement — we'll teach you the industry if you bring the fundamentals
  • Able to travel 40–50% for client meetings, conferences, and industry events
  • The terrority for this role will be within the Eastern Time Zone.

The right person reading this already knows if they're right for it. If that's you — apply.

Compensation: $110,000 base + $125,000 target variable = $235,000 OTE. Uncapped commission plan.

Explore ourwebsite andLinkedIn to learn more about our work and impact.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.excerpt: gravity9 is a boutique IT consulting company headquartered in the UK with offices in the US, Canada, and Poland.
jobs.description:
gravity9 is a boutique IT consulting company headquartered in the UK with offices in the US, Canada, and Poland. Our team has deep experience in engineering, experience design and product management. We enjoy a challenge and pride ourselves on working with our clients on their most complex problems, finding elegant and flexible solutions that help them transform their businesses.

The Role, Honestly

This isn't a job where you own one clean lane. You'll move between product owner, project manager, business analyst, tester, and support engineer — sometimes within the same hour. If you need a title to tell you what you're allowed to touch today, this isn't the right seat. If you'd rather have real ownership over a messy, high-impact problem than a narrow, well-defined one, it might be exactly right.

How This Role Breaks Down

This is directional rather than a weekly timesheet, but it reflects where the role's energy typically goes:

• 30% Product judgment & direction— customer problems, outcomes, prioritization, roadmap tradeoffs

• 30% Delivery & orchestration— backlog, dependencies, workstreams, and getting decisions to shipped software

• 25% Technical problem-solving— APIs, JSON, logs, data flows, troubleshooting, and getting to answers directly

• 15% Stakeholder leadership & communication— alignment, trust, decision-making, and effective collaboration across Poland and U.S. West Coast time zones

What You’ll Actually Do

• Run point across a multi-vendor ecosystem — several platforms, several teams, no single source of truth — and be the person who can explain how they all connect.

• Understand your users deeply enough to represent them accurately when they're not in the room.

• Own the product direction for your area - connect customer needs, business priorities, and technical realities; define the outcomes that matter; and make the tradeoffs needed to keep the roadmap focused.

• Workshop with users and stakeholders — both to turn vague frustration into a clear problem statement, and to shape new features from the ground up.

• Translate business needs into clear requirements, and stay accountable for them all the way through to a working feature — not just a written spec.

• Build and own the backlog, and work directly with developers to turn requirements into shipped software.

• Dig into raw data (JSON payloads, API responses, logs) across multiple systems yourself when you need an answer faster than waiting on someone else's ticket queue.

• Identify and own dependencies across teams and systems — know what's blocking what, and drive it, rather than waiting for someone else to surface it.

• Maintain a clear view across multiple concurrent workstreams, knowing where the important risks, decisions, dependencies, and blockers are - and be able to explain the real status without having to reconstruct it on the spot.

• Build genuine working relationships with the people you depend on — because when you don't own the system, trust is what gets things unblocked.

• Work effectively across time zones - engineering teams are primarily in Poland while client stakeholders are on the U.S. West Coast. You'll need to be deliberate about handoffs, written communication, and making the overlap hours count.

• Act as a fallback layer of technical support on the product when something breaks and the usual path isn't fast enough.

• Say no when something doesn't serve the roadmap, even when it's an easy yes to give.

You’ll Thrive Here If You

• Learn new domains fast and are comfortable operating in one before you've fully mastered it.

• Can hold a strategic view and get into implementation details in the same conversation.

• Are willing to form and share an opinion before you have complete information — and revise it in public when you're wrong.

• Treat ambiguity as the normal condition of the job, not a blocker to raise up the chain.

• Can bring calm and clarity to stakeholders even when the answer isn't obvious yet - and are comfortable saying what you know, what you don't know, and what you'll do next.

This Probably Isn’t A Fit For You If

• You want a job with a fixed scope and a quiet backlog.

• You'd rather escalate ambiguity than sit with it and make a call.

• You need full system access and a clean data model before you're willing to start solving a problem.

Requirements

What We’re Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience in Product Management, Product Ownership, or a similar product delivery role, ideally within a consultancy, SaaS, or complex enterprise environment.

  • Proven experience owning products or major features from discovery through delivery, including requirements, prioritization, backlog management, release planning, and post-launch iteration.

  • Strong ability to translate ambiguous business and customer problems into clear product direction, requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and actionable engineering work.

  • Experience working directly with clients and senior stakeholders, including facilitating discussions, challenging assumptions, managing competing priorities, and driving decisions.

  • Demonstrated ability to partner closely with UX/design and engineering teams to shape solutions rather than simply passing requirements between teams.

  • Experience working with distributed, cross-time-zone teams. This role regularly collaborates with engineering teams in Poland and clients across U.S. time zones, including the West Coast, so flexibility and strong asynchronous communication are essential.

  • Strong understanding of Agile product development, including refinement, sprint planning, dependency management, release coordination, and iterative delivery.

  • Ability to use qualitative and quantitative data to evaluate opportunities, prioritize work, define success measures, and assess product outcomes.

  • Comfortable navigating technical conversations involving APIs, integrations, data flows, third-party systems, and complex enterprise environments.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to create clarity across technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Highly organized and proactive, with the ability to identify gaps, follow through on commitments, surface risks early, and keep work moving without requiring constant direction.

  • Comfortable operating in a consulting environment where priorities can evolve quickly and where Product Managers are expected to bring structure to ambiguity and actively drive outcomes.

  • Candidates must currently reside in, or be willing to relocate at their own expense to the Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill, NC area prior to their start date.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working in a consulting or client-services organization.

  • Experience with consumer-facing digital products, mobile applications, loyalty, hospitality, gaming, e-commerce, or similar customer experience platforms.

  • Familiarity with tools such as Jira, Miro/Mural, Figma, and product analytics platforms.

  • Experience using AI or automation tools as part of product discovery, analysis, requirements development, or delivery workflows.

jobs.description:
Washington Rural Healthcare Case Management, Social Work and Care Coordination Opportunities

Rural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, and community healthcare organizations throughout Washington to identify experienced leaders and professionals in case management, social work, utilization review, discharge planning, and care coordination.

We are currently connecting with professionals who may be interested in active and upcoming case management, social work, utilization management, discharge planning, and care coordination opportunities across Washington.

These opportunities may include positions within Critical Access Hospitals, community hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, Federally Qualified Health Centers, public hospital districts, long-term care organizations, and integrated rural healthcare systems.

This Is More Than a Care Coordination Role

In rural healthcare, helping a patient safely move through the healthcare system often requires creativity, persistence, and strong community relationships.

Case management, social work, and care coordination professionals help connect patients and families with the clinical care, resources, education, and support they need. They may address barriers involving transportation, housing, insurance, behavioral health, long-term care, family support, or access to specialty services far from home.

The strongest professionals understand that a discharge plan is more than paperwork. It is a bridge between the hospital, the patient's home, local providers, community resources, and the next stage of care.

Opportunities May Include

This application may connect you with current or upcoming roles such as:

  • Director or Manager of Case Management
  • Case Management Supervisor
  • Hospital Case Manager
  • Social Work Director or Manager
  • Medical Social Worker
  • Care Coordination Director or Manager
  • Care Coordinator
  • Utilization Review or Utilization Management Director
  • Utilization Review Nurse
  • Discharge Planning Manager
  • Discharge Planner
  • Transitions of Care Manager
  • Population Health Manager
  • Community Health Program Manager
  • Complex Care Manager
  • Patient Navigation leadership
  • Senior case management, social work, or care coordination roles

What You May Lead or Support

Responsibilities will vary by organization and position and may include:

  • Coordinating safe and appropriate patient transitions
  • Developing discharge and follow-up care plans
  • Assessing clinical, social, financial, and community needs
  • Connecting patients and families with local and regional resources
  • Collaborating with physicians, nurses, therapists, behavioral health professionals, and community partners
  • Supporting utilization review, medical necessity, and level-of-care processes
  • Communicating with payers and supporting authorization or denial-management processes
  • Reducing avoidable readmissions and delays in care
  • Supporting patients with complex medical or social needs
  • Coordinating referrals to home health, skilled nursing, rehabilitation, hospice, behavioral health, or specialty care
  • Helping patients navigate insurance, transportation, housing, medication, and other barriers
  • Developing policies, procedures, workflows, and documentation standards
  • Monitoring quality, outcomes, length of stay, and departmental performance
  • Leading, mentoring, and supporting case management or social work teams
  • Building stronger connections between the healthcare organization and the community

What You Will Bring

Qualifications will vary by opportunity, but organizations may seek:

  • Experience in case management, medical social work, utilization review, discharge planning, care coordination, or population health
  • Previous leadership experience for director, manager, or supervisory opportunities
  • Knowledge of healthcare delivery, payer requirements, medical necessity, and patient transitions
  • Experience working with patients and families facing complex clinical or social needs
  • Strong communication, assessment, advocacy, and problem-solving skills
  • The ability to collaborate across clinical, operational, and community teams
  • Experience with rural hospitals, Critical Access Hospitals, FQHCs, public hospital districts, long-term care, or community healthcare organizations
  • Relevant education, licensure, or certification based on the position
  • A compassionate, resourceful, and relationship-focused approach

Some opportunities may require or prefer credentials such as RN, LICSW, LSWAIC, MSW, ACM, CCM, or another case management, nursing, or social work credential. Requirements will depend on the specific position.

Why Rural Washington?

Washington's rural healthcare organizations serve communities surrounded by mountains, forests, farmland, rivers, islands, and coastlines. Distance, limited transportation, workforce shortages, and fewer local services can make care transitions especially challenging.

Working in case management, social work, or care coordination in a rural setting offers the opportunity to help patients overcome real barriers, strengthen community connections, and make care feel more coordinated and humane.

Join the RSS Rural Talent Network

By applying through this page, you are joining the confidential Rural Staffing Services talent network. You may be considered for current or upcoming case management, social work, utilization review, discharge planning, and care coordination opportunities that align with your experience, goals, preferred location, and availability.

  • Which Washington communities or regions you would consider
  • Whether you are open to relocation

Our team personally reviews each application. When we identify an opportunity that may be a strong match, we will contact you directly to share more about the organization, community, position, and next steps.

Your information will be handled professionally and confidentially.

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Regulatory Affairs Director - Inflammation and Rare Disease

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. Amgen is seeking a Regulatory Affairs Director supporting products in the Inflammation and Rare Disease Therapeutic Area. Global Regulatory Affairs (GRA) provides global regulatory leadership, expertise, and execution for the development, registration, and life cycle management of all Amgen molecules.

In this vital, product-facing role you will lead the Global Regulatory Team (GRT) in the Regulatory Affairs organization. The role of the Regulatory Affairs Director is to lead GRTs within Amgen’s GRAAS organization, develop a comprehensive regulatory strategy that takes into account worldwide regulatory requirements to drive product development, global registration, achievement and maintenance of desired regional labeling, and effective regulatory agency interactions, and to provide regulatory expertise and guidance to product teams.

jobs.description:
Statut :Régulier, temps plein

Satus : Regular, full-time

(English to follow)


Gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies

Secteur hospitalier et produits biosimilaires, Pfizer Canada | Québec)

Objectif

Joignez-vous à une toute nouvelle fonction au cœur de l’avenir du Secteur hospitalier et produits biosimilaires (SHPBMM) de Pfizer au Canada. Alors que nous élargissons notre gamme de produits multisources et biosimilaires, le canal de vente au détail de produits pharmaceutiques prend de plus en plus d’importance, et il est essentiel d’entretenir des liens solides avec les pharmacies de détail pour améliorer l’accès des patient·e·s à nos médicaments.

En tant que titulaire de l’un des deux nouveaux postes de gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies, le ou la gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies pour l’Ontario mettra en œuvre nos priorités en matière de vente au détail au niveau des comptes, en commençant par les produits biosimilaires destinés aux soins de soutien, où c’est la décision de la pharmacie quant à la délivrance, et non la prescription seule, qui détermine quel médicament le patient ou la patiente reçoit. Vous travaillerez en complément des gestionnaires – Clients institutionnels, qui continueront de se concentrer sur les établissements, et vous relèverez de votre chef – Affaires régionales.

Le ou la gestionnaire – Comptes pharmacies pour l’Ontario relève du ou de la chef – Affaires régionales pour l’Ontario

Fonctions principales

  • Établir et entretenir des relations de confiance à long terme avec les principales parties prenantes responsables de décisions et celles qui exercent une influence au sein des comptes clés de pharmacie au détail, notamment les sièges sociaux et les équipes d’achat, les propriétaires de pharmacies, les pharmacien·ne·s et les membres du personnel des pharmacies.
  • Accroître la présence et la disponibilité des produits de Pfizer dans le canal de vente au détail de produits pharmaceutiques afin que les ordonnances de produits biosimilaires de Pfizer puissent se traduire par la distribution de produits de Pfizer.
  • Cibler et hiérarchiser les comptes de pharmacies de détail en fonction du volume de délivrance et des possibilités de croissance pour la gamme de produits du SHPBMM, en privilégiant dans un premier temps les produits biosimilaires destinés aux soins de soutien.
  • En collaboration avec les gestionnaires – Clients institutionnels, les autres gestionnaires – Comptes pharmacies et votre chef – Affaires régionales, élaborer et mettre en œuvre des stratégies de compte et des plans d’affaires pour les comptes prioritaires de pharmacies de détail dans votre territoire, conformément avec la stratégie du SHPBMM au Canada et des besoins de chaque compte.
  • Acquérir une compréhension approfondie des objectifs, stratégies et priorités de chaque client·e, notamment ses pratiques en matière d’achat, de stocks, de délivrance et de substitution, et l’appliquer à la planification de comptes afin d’élaborer une analyse de rentabilité convaincante qui se traduira par un plan d’action convenu et mis en œuvre.
  • Élaborer des approches commerciales et des offres de comptes spécifiques pour ce canal qui soient compétitives et réactives, en collaboration avec les groupes Marketing, Contrats, Approvisionnement, Accès au marché, Affaires juridiques et Conformité, tout en respectant en tout temps les politiques de l’entreprise et les réglementations en vigueur.
  • Maintenir une connaissance pratique des milieux des payeurs provinciaux et privés de votre province en ce qui concerne leur incidence sur les pratiques de délivrance des pharmacies de détail et l’adoption des produits biosimilaires pour vous permettre de prendre des décisions commerciales éclairées.
  • Collaborer étroitement avec les représentant·e·s en soins de santé virtuels, le ou la chef – Services de soutien aux patient·e·s sur le terrain, les premier·ère·s partenaires stratégiques, le Marketing, le programme de soutien aux patients, et d’autres collègues sur le terrain et au siège social afin d’assurer une approche coordonnée et sans chevauchement au sein des écosystèmes communautaires, institutionnels et de vente au détail, et d’atteindre les objectifs de vente pour les produits du SHPBMM de la gamme qui lui est attribuée.
  • Recueillir et partager des informations sur les tendances du canal des produits pharmaceutiques de détail, les activités des concurrents dans le marché des produits biosimilaires multisources ainsi que les résultats en matière de ventes et de parts de marché au niveau des comptes, puis transmettre ces informations à la direction des équipes du SHPBMM, du Marketing et des marques.
  • Analyser les activités des comptes, suivre les progrès accomplis par rapport aux plans de comptes et aux objectifs du canal, et ajuster les plans d’action et l’attribution des ressources au besoin.
  • Coordonner et mettre en œuvre des programmes de formation conformes pour la clientèle des produits pharmaceutiques de détail, participer aux congrès et événements pertinents et exploiter les ressources de Pfizer au profit de segments de clientèle clés.
  • Faire des recommandations et contribuer à l’affectation des ressources de Pfizer au sein des différents comptes selon les besoins.
  • Mettre à profit différents canaux et privilégier le numérique, en démontrant une forte capacité et un déploiement efficace des technologies et des canaux numériques, afin d’améliorer l’expérience client, d’optimiser l’efficacité du personnel et de garantir un accès optimal des patient·e·s à nos médicaments.
  • Assurer une conformité complète de toutes les activités commerciales et déclarer les manifestations indésirables et les plaintes relatives aux produits, conformément aux procédures de l’entreprise.

Qualifications

  • Diplôme universitaire en administration ou en sciences, et cinq ans d’expérience au minimum dans la vente de produits pharmaceutiques.
  • Succès éprouvé dans des postes nécessitant des interactions avec la clientèle, de préférence en gestion des comptes de pharmacie de détail.
  • Compétences avérées en gestion de comptes et en vente, assorties de la capacité à cibler des occasions permettant d’atteindre les objectifs de Pfizer et de la clientèle.
  • Solide sens des affaires et capacités de gestion stratégique, avec maîtrise des outils de gestion des relations avec la clientèle et d’analyse ainsi que de Microsoft Office.
  • Excellentes aptitudes pour la communication, la présentation d’exposés, la négociation et les relations interpersonnelles.
  • Réseau établi de parties prenantes clés dans le canal de vente au détail de produits pharmaceutiques, un atout.
  • Expérience dans le domaine des médicaments génériques, des produits biosimilaires et d’autres produits multisources, un atout.
  • Expérience en matière d’établissement de contrats, de tarification ou de négociation commerciale, un atout
  • Capacité à voyager fréquemment en Ontario et à détenir un permis de conduire valide

Compétences linguistiques

  • Excellentes aptitudes pour la communication orale et écrite en anglais.

Le salaire annuel de base pour ce poste varie de 107,925 $ à 179,875$.

L’échelle salariale fournie s’applique seulement au Canada, et ne s’applique à aucun autre endroit à l’extérieur du Canada.

Pharmacy Key Account Manager (PKAM)


Pfizer GH&B Canada | Quebec


Purpose

Join a brand-new capability at the heart of Pfizer GH&B Canada's future. As we evolve toward a broader multisource and biosimilars portfolio, the retail pharmacy channel is becoming increasingly important, and strong relationships with retail pharmacies are key to increasing patient access to our medications.

As one of two newly created Pharmacy Key Account Managers (PKAMs), the Ontario PKAM will turn our retail priorities into execution at the account level, starting with supportive care biosimilars, where the pharmacy's dispensing decision, not the prescription alone, determines which product the patient receives. You will complement the Institutional Key Account Managers (IKAMs), who remain focused on institutions, and report to your Regional Business Manager (RBM).

The Ontario PKAM reports to the Ontario RBM.
