A Day in Your Life at MKS:

As a Principal Business Systems Analyst at MKS, Inc. you will partner with business and IT partners to gather business intelligence reporting and analytic requirements, write functional specification documents to map data from applications, create report & dashboard wireframes, conduct detailed source data analysis, identify data gaps and work with the business and technical teams to implement high-quality BI solutions. In this role, you will report to the Sr. Manager of Data Warehouse and Business Intelligence Reporting.

You Will Make an Impact By:

· Partnering with business stakeholders and cross-functional teams to gather, analyze, and document reporting and analytics requirements, translating business needs into functional specifications, user stories, and technical report designs.

· Designing, developing, testing, and implementing data and reporting solutions that support enterprise-wide business intelligence and analytics initiatives.

· Leading requirements definition, business process analysis, and documentation efforts, including Business Requirements Documents (BRDs) and Functional Specification Documents (FSDs), while obtaining stakeholder alignment and approval.

· Collaborating with project managers, architects, and technical teams to define solution roadmaps, delivery plans, and reporting strategies that align with organizational objectives.

· Leading testing activities, including integration testing and user acceptance testing (UAT), documenting test plans, managing issue resolution, and ensuring successful solution deployment.

· Serving as a subject matter expert for reporting and analytics solutions by troubleshooting data and reporting issues, validating data integrity, improving business processes, and delivering end-user training to drive adoption of BI capabilities.


Skills You Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of progressive experience in IT, systems/data analysis, and SAP data warehouse environments.
  • Strong understanding of data warehouse and ETL processes with ability to write SQL queries to analyze data; Experience working with SAP BW, SAP BW on HANA, SAP ECC, ORACLE or other major ERP systems.

jobs.excerpt: Washington Rural Behavioral Health Leadership OpportunitiesRural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, community health centers, and behavioral health organizations throughout Washington to identify experienced leaders who understand the unique challenges and opportunities of serving rural communities.
jobs.description:
Washington Rural Behavioral Health Leadership Opportunities

Rural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, community health centers, and behavioral health organizations throughout Washington to identify experienced leaders who understand the unique challenges and opportunities of serving rural communities.

We are currently connecting with professionals who may be interested in active and upcoming behavioral health leadership opportunities across Washington.

These opportunities may include leadership within Critical Access Hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, Federally Qualified Health Centers, community hospitals, integrated care programs, outpatient behavioral health clinics, substance-use treatment programs, crisis services, and community-based organizations.

This Is More Than a Behavioral Health Role

Behavioral health access can be especially limited in rural communities, making strong leadership essential.

Behavioral health leaders help organizations build programs that are accessible, sustainable, compassionate, and responsive to the needs of the community. They may lead mental health, substance-use, crisis response, social services, or integrated behavioral health programs while working closely with clinical, operational, and community partners.

The strongest leaders understand that behavioral health care does not exist in isolation. It is connected to primary care, emergency services, social needs, housing, transportation, workforce shortages, and the overall well-being of the community.

Rural behavioral health leadership requires creativity, collaboration, cultural awareness, and a genuine commitment to meeting people where they are.

Opportunities May Include

This application may connect you with current or upcoming roles such as:

  • Behavioral Health Director
  • Director of Mental Health Services
  • Behavioral Health Program Manager
  • Integrated Behavioral Health Director or Manager
  • Substance Use Disorder Program Director
  • Crisis Services Director or Manager
  • Community Behavioral Health Manager
  • Psychiatric Services Director
  • Clinical Director of Behavioral Health
  • Social Services Director
  • Counseling Services Manager
  • Care Integration or Population Health leadership
  • Behavioral Health Operations leadership

What You May Lead

Responsibilities will vary by organization and position and may include:

  • Providing strategic and operational leadership for behavioral health services
  • Developing, expanding, or strengthening mental health and substance-use programs
  • Supporting integrated behavioral health within primary care or hospital settings
  • Leading clinical and nonclinical behavioral health teams
  • Recruiting, developing, and retaining behavioral health professionals
  • Strengthening access to care in rural and underserved communities
  • Supporting crisis response, suicide prevention, and care-transition programs
  • Building relationships with schools, law enforcement, tribal partners, public agencies, and community organizations
  • Overseeing program quality, compliance, documentation, and regulatory readiness
  • Managing budgets, grants, contracts, staffing, and program performance
  • Developing policies, procedures, workflows, and service-delivery models
  • Supporting telebehavioral health and other creative access solutions
  • Tracking outcomes and using data to improve care and program sustainability
  • Advocating for patients, families, employees, and the communities being served

What You Will Bring

Qualifications will vary by opportunity, but organizations may seek:

  • Progressive experience in behavioral health, mental health, substance-use treatment, social services, or integrated care
  • Previous leadership experience as a director, manager, clinical supervisor, program administrator, or comparable leader
  • Experience developing, managing, or improving behavioral health programs
  • Knowledge of behavioral health regulations, documentation, quality standards, and reimbursement
  • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams
  • Strong communication, relationship-building, and problem-solving skills
  • Experience working with rural, underserved, or high-need populations
  • Familiarity with hospitals, FQHCs, Rural Health Clinics, community behavioral health organizations, or public agencies
  • Relevant education, licensure, or certification based on the specific position
  • A compassionate, collaborative, and community-focused leadership style

Some opportunities may prefer or require licensure such as LICSW, LMHC, LMFT, SUDP, psychologist, psychiatric nurse practitioner, or another behavioral health credential. Requirements will depend on the specific role.

Why Rural Washington?

Washington's rural communities are surrounded by mountains, forests, farmland, rivers, islands, and coastlines, but distance and workforce shortages can make behavioral health services difficult to access.

Leading behavioral health in a rural setting offers the opportunity to build meaningful programs, form lasting community partnerships, and help ensure people can receive care close to home.

The impact of this work may be felt not only by patients, but also by families, schools, employers, healthcare teams, and the broader community.

Join the RSS Rural Talent Network

By applying through this page, you are joining the confidential Rural Staffing Services talent network. You may be considered for current or upcoming behavioral health leadership opportunities that align with your experience, goals, location preferences, and availability.

Please submit your resume and let us know:

  • Which Washington communities or regions you would consider
  • Whether you are open to relocation
  • Whether you are interested in permanent, interim, remote, or multiple types of opportunities
  • Which position or community you were viewing on RSSJobs.org

Our team personally reviews each application. When we identify an opportunity that may be a strong match, we will contact you directly to share more about the organization, community, program needs, and next steps.

Your information will be handled professionally and confidentially.

Work Where It Matters.

Backblaze is the object storage leader in the open cloud movement, fueling customer success with cloud storage built purposefully to unlock budgets, unburden administrators, and unleash innovators. Want to know what you’ll be doing?

You will work on our data infrastructure platform which supports the B2 Object Storage and Computer Backup products, responsible for the data infrastructure that everything runs on. You will help improve automation, observability and stability for durability, increase throughput, and drive architectural changes to support the long term requirements of our service.

  • Build reporting, dashboards, and visualizations that give engineering and leadership a clear view into fleet health, capacity, and operational trends
  • Build system health tooling that detects failing hardware, drifting configuration, and capacity risk before they turn into incidents
  • Lead technical design discussions and produce clear design documents for changes that span multiple services and teams
  • Drive the implementation of large features from design through rollout, including the migration and backfill work that real systems require
  • Partner with the on-call rotation to turn recurring toil and incident findings into automation and better signal

The Right Fit:

  • 7+ years of backend development in an enterprise environment, working in an object-oriented or systems language (Java, Rust, C++, C#, Go, or similar)
  • Experience designing automation frameworks or platforms that other engineers build on
  • Experience building large scale software systems running on thousands of servers

  • Working knowledge of an observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, ELK, Datadog, or equivalent), including instrumenting a service and designing alerts people trust

  • Experience with discovering and implementing performance improvements, including CPU and IO

jobs.excerpt: About IFS LogisticsIFS Logistics (built and launched as 7bridges, now part of IFS) is an AI-native enterprise logistics platform.
jobs.description:
About IFS Logistics

IFS Logistics (built and launched as 7bridges, now part of IFS) is an AI-native enterprise logistics platform. We unify transport data, optimise carrier spend, and automate execution for enterprise shippers and logistics companies. We are a small, dedicated product and engineering team inside IFS, reporting into the commercial organisation rather than central R&D. Pure SaaS, zero consultancy: if a customer needs us to operate the software for them, we have failed.

The role

This is not a traditional "add AI to an existing system" role. You will set the technical direction for our Experience squad — the layer where the whole platform meets the customer: SSO and identity, IFS Intelligence integration, the demo environment, and the cross-product surface that ties Data Connect, TPAO, Shipper TMS and Revenue Protect into one product.

The squad does not exist yet. You will help build it, set its architecture and standards, and be accountable for what it ships. You stay hands-on — this is not a management-only role. You are the squad's technical voice to the VP Product and Chief Architect.

Your depth is backend and platform. Every engineer here is expected to be genuinely fullstack; the profile describes where your depth is, not a boundary you stay inside. You will review React as readily as Django.

What you'll work on

  • API v3 and the service boundaries that let four product areas share one identity, permission and navigation model without a shared mess.
  • SSO, tenancy and permissions done once, properly — "all data visible by default, restricted only by exception".
  • A demo environment that is a real product surface, not a fixture — commercially load-bearing and used every week.
  • IFS Intelligence and IFS Cloud integration, including the embedding path opened up by Project Oliver.
  • Where the agent sits in each new surface, and the guardrails, observability and cost controls that make agentic behaviour safe to ship.

What we're looking for

  • Around eight years or more building and running production software, with real depth in Python/Django REST API design, data modelling and service reliability.
  • You have set technical direction for a team: chosen the approach, written it down, defended it, and changed it when you were wrong.
  • Strong on performance, cost and observability. You have owned the pager as well as the design doc.
  • Genuinely fullstack — comfortable in React and able to raise the bar on frontend work you do not write yourself.
  • You raise other people's standards. Review, pairing and honest feedback are things you do by default.
  • AI-native in practice: you build with Cursor and Claude daily, you know how to give an agent the right context, and you can tell when its output is wrong.
  • You form and state a view. Ambiguity is the job, not a blocker.

Nice to have

  • Multi-tenant enterprise SaaS, SSO/identity, or ERP integration experience.
  • LLM agent orchestration, RAG or evals in production.
  • Shipped agents into a product for real work, like agentic audit or agent-managed fulfilment rules, with a view on where an agent earns its place and where it does not.
  • Simulation or scenario modelling: synthetic data or replay used to prove out logic before it ships.
  • BigQuery, dbt, Pub/Sub, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform.
  • Logistics, supply chain or freight.

Tech stack

Python (Django REST), TypeScript/Node, React · BigQuery, dbt, Cube Cloud, Superset · Pub/Sub, Datastream · GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, GitLab CI/CD · LLMs, RAG, agent frameworks, evals · Cursor + Claude, Notion (SDD Central), Jira.

What success looks like — first 6 months

  • The Experience squad has a written technical approach that the rest of engineering uses as a reference point.
  • API v3 surfaces owned by the squad are in production, observable, and within cost budget.
  • SSO and cross-product permissions are shipped and self-serve.
  • Code review on all merge requests and no direct-to-prod are real in your squad, not aspirational.
  • The engineers in the squad are visibly better than when they joined.

Why this role exists now

We are shifting from feature-driven engineering to agent-led product architecture. The Experience layer is where that shift is most visible and where it currently hurts most: navigation has crept, data is hidden that should not be, and agent-first thinking is not yet applied systematically. That gap is the job. We are honest about it — and we need someone who will set the direction rather than wait for one.

You'll need to be based in either the UK or the Netherlands - we're a remote team with clusters of people in London and Amsterdam.

We embrace flexibility and hybrid work opportunities to support diverse needs and lifestyles, while also valuing inclusive workplace experiences. By fostering a sense of community, we drive innovation, strengthen connections, and nurture belonging. Our commitment ensures you can work in a way that suits you best, while also engaging with colleagues to share ideas and build meaningful relationships.

IFS is a billion-dollar revenue company with 7000+ employees on all continents. Our leading AI technology is the backbone of our award-winning enterprise software solutions, enabling our customers to be their best when it really matters–at the Moment of Service™. Our commitment to internal AI adoption has allowed us to stay at the forefront of technological advancements, ensuring our colleagues can unlock their creativity and productivity, and our solutions are always cutting-edge.

At IFS, we’re flexible, we’re innovative, and we’re focused not only on how we can engage with our customers but on how we can make a real change and have a worldwide impact. We help solve some of society’s greatest challenges, fostering a better future through our agility, collaboration, and trust.

We celebrate diversity and understand our responsibility to reflect the diverse world we work in. We are committed to promoting an inclusive workforce that fully represents the many different cultures, backgrounds, and viewpoints of our customers, our partners, and our communities. As a truly international company serving people from around the globe, we realize that our success is tantamount to the respect we have for those different points of view.

By joining our team, you will have the opportunity to be part of a global, diverse environment; you will be joining a winning team with a commitment to sustainability; and a company where we get things done so that you can make a positive impact on the world.

We’re looking for innovative and original thinkers to work in an environment where you can #MakeYourMoment so that we can help others make theirs. With the power of our AI-driven solutions, we empower our team to change the status quo and make a real difference.

If you want to change the status quo, we’ll help you make your moment. Join Team Purple. Join IFS.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

Compensation and Benefits

We use a systematic compensation framework: salary scales are set each year for each job vertical, managers level folks on their team, and those levels are mapped directly to our compensation scales. A location-based adjustment is applied outside of SF and NYC (typically 5-10%) - feel free to ask us about your location!
Given the systematic approach, we always make First and Best offers - there is no negotiation (for new hires nor our existing teammates). This ensures people are paid based on their expected contribution, not their negotiation skills.
We offer top-notch health care plans, with 100% of the premiums covered for medical, dental, and vision for employees.
We offer flexible PTO, with a norm of taking off about 6 weeks per year (including federal holidays). We also provide home office equipment, a professional development stipend, and free food at our offices.
